title: Artificial Intelligence Ethics
text: AI ethics is the branch of applied ethics that examines the moral implications of developing and deploying artificial intelligence. Key concerns include algorithmic bias (AI systems that perpetuate or amplify human biases), privacy (AI's ability to process vast personal data), transparency and explainability (the 'black box' problem), accountability for AI decisions, job displacement, autonomous weapons, and existential risk from advanced AI systems. Regulatory frameworks are emerging, including the EU AI Act (2024), which classifies AI applications by risk level and imposes obligations on high-risk systems. Major AI labs have published ethical guidelines and safety research programs. The debate between effective accelerationism and AI safety is prominent in the field.
